covered_sources.title: Capable language models can outgrow the benefits of collaboration
More Agents Is All You Need
Scaling Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Collaboration
When collaboration fails: persuasion driven adversarial influence in multi agent large language model debate
Mixture-of-Agents Enhances Large Language Model Capabilities
Rethinking Mixture-of-Agents: Is Mixing Different Large Language Models Beneficial?
Population Based Training of Neural Networks

mechanism_findings.evidence: Across 260 matched-compute configurations spanning six agentic benchmarks, five architectures and three LLM families, the 2026 Nature Machine Intelligence study found MAS gains ranged from +80.8% on structured financial reasoning to -70.0% on sequential planning. Single-agent baseline performance was the strongest robust predictor; an approximately 45% baseline threshold predicted zero-to-negative MAS gains and matched the sign of MAS gain in 94% of 16 SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench validation configurations. Centralized verification reduced error amplification to 4.4x versus 17.2x for independent MAS.
mechanism_findings.decision_relevance: Do not treat parallelism as a universal default. Route tasks to multi-agent only when decomposable/parallelizable or when single-agent baseline is weak; preserve a centralized validation bottleneck when agents share conclusions.
mechanism_findings.scope: Empirical rule validated within the tested model families, benchmarks and matched per-system compute ceilings; authors explicitly caution against treating the ~45% threshold as universal.

mechanism_findings.evidence: Agent Forest reports monotonic performance gains as ensemble size increases across GSM8K, MATH, MMLU, Chess and HumanEval. On GSM8K, a 40-sample Llama2-13B ensemble reached 59% versus 35% for a single sample and exceeded a single Llama2-70B at 54%; gains were larger on harder tasks and weaker models.
mechanism_findings.decision_relevance: For separable candidate generation, cheap independent parallel samples with a simple aggregator can outperform a more complex interactive debate, especially when base-model accuracy is modest.
mechanism_findings.scope: Mostly static/non-agentic benchmarks; should not be generalized to long-horizon tool-using workflows because 2026 controlled agentic evidence shows qualitatively different scaling.

mechanism_findings.evidence: MacNet supports collaboration among more than 1,000 agents and reports irregular/small-world-like DAG topologies outperforming regular ones, with normalized solution quality following a logistic growth curve as agent count scales.
mechanism_findings.decision_relevance: If large parallel populations are used, topology matters; avoid assuming fully connected debate or isolated workers are optimal. Test sparse irregular DAGs with bounded communication and an explicit aggregator.
mechanism_findings.scope: ICLR 2025 evaluation context; exact transfer to O requires matched ablation under O tasks and budget.

mechanism_findings.evidence: A 2026 Scientific Reports study found one persuasion-optimized adversarial agent could reduce group accuracy by 10-40% and increase incorrect consensus by >30%. More agents or debate rounds did not reliably fix the problem; RAG and Best-of-N could amplify attack credibility. Retrieval-config ablations still showed average accuracy drops around 18-24%.
mechanism_findings.decision_relevance: Do not allow peer consensus or rhetorical confidence to directly determine adoption. Evidence/provenance checks and a verifier insulated from peer persuasion are more important than adding debate rounds.
mechanism_findings.scope: Adversarial debate settings on TruthfulQA, MMLU, MedMCQA and SCALR; this is a robustness result, not evidence that all debate is harmful.

mechanism_findings.evidence: Self-MoA reports that using multiple outputs from the single strongest model outperformed mixed-model MoA by 6.6% on AlpacaEval 2.0 and by 3.8% on average across MMLU, CRUX and MATH. The paper attributes this to a quality-diversity trade-off: mixing weaker heterogeneous proposers can lower ensemble quality.
mechanism_findings.decision_relevance: Diversity should not be bought by injecting weaker agents indiscriminately. Prefer independent contexts/prompts/seeds from a strong model, and add heterogeneous agents only when they contribute demonstrably complementary competence.
mechanism_findings.scope: MoA-style static inference benchmarks; not yet evidence for persistent autonomous research workers.

mechanism_findings.evidence: DeepMind PBT trains populations in parallel while periodically copying promising parameters and mutating hyperparameters. Reported examples include DM Lab human-normalized 0.93->1.06, Atari 1.47->1.81, StarCraft II 0.36->0.39, WMT14 En-De BLEU 22.30->22.65 and CIFAR-10 GAN Inception 6.45->6.89, while running in the time of a single training run rather than sequential tuning.
mechanism_findings.decision_relevance: For expensive adaptive experiments, exploit/explore with periodic inheritance can turn otherwise wasted parallel runs into a directed search process. Candidate for research-strategy optimization, but requires careful contamination controls when applied to scientific agents.
mechanism_findings.scope: Training/hyperparameter optimization, not inference-time LLM agent collaboration.

dead_ends_or_cautions: Static benchmark agent-count scaling is not sufficient evidence for long-horizon autonomous agent scaling.
More debate rounds and more agents are not reliable robustness mechanisms under persuasive/adversarial influence.
Heterogeneous model mixing can hurt if diversity comes from lower-quality proposers.
The Nature 2026 ~45% capability threshold is a validated within-domain selection rule, not a universal law.
